hero.eyebrow: v0.4.0 · open source · packaged for Kubernetes
hero.title: Give agents useful reach.
hero.lede: Run self-hosted AI agents on hardware you own. Dekopon gives models a capable workspace while a separate broker controls identity, permissions, credentials, outside I/O, and audit.
hero.caveat: A substantial, testable local foundation for small hardware. Dekopon is still pre-production and its Kubernetes deployment uses one Unix UID trust domain.

title: Useful agents.
No ambient power.
pillars.intro: Dekopon combines a familiar model workspace with strict process boundaries. The model can plan and ask; owner-controlled infrastructure decides and executes.

items.title: Deploy on hardware you own.
items.body: Run four compact executables on Linux or macOS. The v0.4.0 image supports arm64 and amd64, and the Helm chart is designed for a single-node Raspberry Pi-class cluster.

items.title: Say exactly who may act.
items.body: Cedar matches a trusted principal, one action, one resource, and broker-derived context. Separate constraint sets cap the destination, method, calls, bytes, credential, and time.

items.title: Use shell fluency without a shell account.
items.body: The model receives one homemade bash-flavored tool. It can inspect and combine granted capabilities, but cannot start a process, read a file, inherit an environment, or open a socket.

items.title: Follow the whole run.
items.body: One trace follows a chat message through model turns, scripts, policy, provider work, and HTTP. Durable broker audit separately records what was authorized.

concepts.title: The homepage is the map. These guides are the territory.
concepts.intro: Each guide stands on its own, uses the code that ships in v0.4.0, and ends with a link to the latest implementation contract.

items.label: Trusted identity
items.title: A gateway can vouch. It cannot mint authority.
items.body: See how an authenticated chat sender becomes a canonical subject, then a broker-mapped principal and Cedar context.

items.label: Cedar permissions
items.title: Principal. Action. Resource. Context.
items.body: Build a complete PR-commenter policy and keep execution limits and credentials beyond policy’s reach.

items.label: One-tool runtime
items.title: A familiar dark room with locked doors.
items.body: Learn how models use shell habits, capability discovery, jq, loops, and exit codes inside a homemade interpreter.

items.label: OpenTelemetry
items.title: One message. Three processes. One waterfall.
items.body: Read a trace from gateway to model to broker and understand why audit, traces, and logs remain separate.

items.label: Models & memory
items.title: A conversation grows. The model starts fresh.
items.body: Follow request context across model and Slack turns, then separate prompt-cache hints, bounded conversation history, and long-term memory.

deployment.title: From release archive to a Kubernetes pod.
deployment.intro: Version 0.4.0 changes distribution, not authority. The same separated gateway and broker now ship in a verified multi-architecture image and a security-conscious Helm chart.
points: A native broker sidecar becomes ready before the gateway starts
An init container creates real owner-only files from Kubernetes projections
Audit and checkpoint state stay together on one persistent volume
Provider and model credentials never enter the image

closing.title: Let the model explore.
closing.body: Bring a model, narrow capabilities, and hardware you own. Dekopon gives agents a useful place to work without handing them the keys to the host.
